# Add unit coverage for the Email, Url and ZipCode form fields

> **New here? This issue is written to be finishable on a clean clone.** You need Node, a fork and an evening. No Docker, no API key, no AI service, nothing beyond `npm install`. If anything below turns out to need more than that, say so in a comment — that is a bug in the issue, not in you.

## Context

Neo ships three form fields whose entire reason to exist is a validation rule: `Neo.form.field.Email`, `Neo.form.field.Url` and `Neo.form.field.ZipCode`. Measured on 2026-09-19 at `dev@afddc57634`: **no file under `test/playwright/` references any of the three** — not by import, not by class name.

Their sibling `Neo.form.field.Phone` is the counter-example. It has `test/playwright/unit/form/field/PhoneInputPatternReDoS.spec.mjs`, which pins both what its pattern accepts *and* how fast it decides. That spec is the shape this issue asks you to bring to the other three.

## The Problem

A validation rule with no test is a rule that can be widened by accident. Someone rewrites a regex to accept one more legitimate address, and nothing tells them it now also accepts a malformed one — the field keeps looking correct, because a field that accepts everything looks exactly like a field that is working.

There is a second thing worth pinning here, and it is the more interesting half: **the three fields do not validate the same way.**

- `Email` overrides `validate()` (`src/form/field/Email.mjs:43`) and tests `Email.emailRegex` itself, setting `errorTextValidEmail` on failure.
- `Url` sets a default `inputPattern` (`src/form/field/Url.mjs:29`) and lets the base class in `src/form/field/Text.mjs` apply it, with `errorTextInputPattern` as the message.
- `ZipCode` swaps its `inputPattern` per country (`src/form/field/ZipCode.mjs:64`), from a static `countryCodes` map that currently holds `AT`, `CH` and `DE` only.

Same user-visible outcome, three different code paths. Nothing currently asserts that they agree about what "invalid" means.

## The Architectural Reality

| field | file | validation mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| `Neo.form.field.Email` | `src/form/field/Email.mjs` | own `validate()` override + `static emailRegex` |
| `Neo.form.field.Url` | `src/form/field/Url.mjs` | default `inputPattern`, applied by `Neo.form.field.Text` |
| `Neo.form.field.ZipCode` | `src/form/field/ZipCode.mjs` | `inputPattern` reassigned from `static countryCodes[countryCode]` |

All three extend `Neo.form.field.Text`. `validate(silent)` returns a `Boolean` and, when `silent` is `false` and the field is not `clean`, also pushes the error text through `updateError()`. Validation runs in the App Worker — no DOM needed, which is why this belongs in the unit tier.

## The Fix

Add specs under `test/playwright/unit/form/field/`. One file per field is fine, and so is one file for all three — your call, say which you chose and why in the PR.

Copy the header from `test/playwright/unit/form/field/PhoneInputPatternReDoS.spec.mjs`: the `setup()` call with its `neoConfig` block comes **before** the other imports, and the field is created with `Neo.create(Email, {appName})`. That is how the class system and the app context get initialised for the unit tier; a plain `new Email()` will not work.

**What to assert**

- **Accepts and rejects.** For each field, a list of values that must pass and a list that must fail, each written out literally. Aim for the boundary, not the obvious middle: for `Email`, an address with a subdomain and one with a trailing dot; for `Url`, a bare host, an `https://` host, a path, and something with a space in it; for `ZipCode`, a valid `DE` code and a four-digit one that `DE` must reject but `AT` must accept.
- **`ZipCode` follows its country.** Set `countryCode` to `AT`, then to `DE`, and assert the same input changes verdict. `countryCodes` holds `AT`, `CH` and `DE`; what happens for a country that is **not** in the map is worth asserting too — read `:64` and pin the behaviour you find there.
- **Empty is not invalid.** All three sit on top of `Text`, where `required` is the config that makes a field mandatory. Assert that an empty value alone does not fail validation unless `required` says so.
- **`validate(false)` sets the error text**, and `validate(true)` does not, for at least one of the three. The error strings are `errorTextValidEmail` and `errorTextInputPattern`.

If you find a case where one field's answer contradicts another's for the same kind of input, that is the most valuable thing you can put in the PR body. Do not fix it here — report it.

## How to run it

```bash
npm install
npx playwright test -c test/playwright/playwright.config.unit.mjs test/playwright/unit/form/field/
```

The whole unit tier is `npm run test-unit`. **Do not run a bare `npx playwright test`** — this repository has several Playwright configurations and the default one is not the unit tier.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] New spec or specs under `test/playwright/unit/form/field/` cover all three fields, following the `setup()`-first shape of the existing specs in that directory.
- [ ] Each field has both an accepted set and a rejected set, with the values written out literally.
- [ ] `ZipCode` is asserted against at least two different `countryCode` values, and the not-in-the-map case is pinned to whatever the source actually does.
- [ ] At least one assertion covers `validate(false)` producing the error text.
- [ ] The specs pass on the unit configuration, and the PR body says how you ran them.
- [ ] No file under `src/` is changed. If an assertion goes red against a field, say so in the PR — that finding becomes its own issue, with your test as its evidence.

## Out of Scope

- Changing any validation rule or regex. This issue pins the current behaviour; changing it is a separate conversation.
- Adding countries to `ZipCode.countryCodes`.
- Rendering the fields or testing their DOM. This is the unit tier; `Neo.form.field.Phone`'s spec shows how much can be asserted without a browser.
- `Neo.form.field.Phone` itself, which already has the coverage this issue is modelled on.

## Before you open the PR

- Branch from `dev` and target `dev` — not `main`.
- Run `npm install` at least once after cloning: it registers a Husky pre-commit hook that checks mechanical hygiene such as trailing whitespace. Committing without it will fail CI on something unrelated to your test.
- <https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/dev/CONTRIBUTING.md> has the rest.
